summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 25%), ICD, chronic kidney disease, and a right humeral fracture was admitted for acute shortness of breath worsening when lying flat, consistent with fluid overload from heart failure exacerbation. Evaluation showed minimal pulmonary edema on chest X-ray, elevated BNP, and no acute ischemia. He was treated with IV furosemide and transitioned to increased oral torsemide. His diabetes was managed with insulin during admission due to elevated blood glucose, and he was restarted on glipizide at discharge. Insomnia and depression were addressed with continuation of imipramine and perphenazine, and initiation of mirtazapine. Subtherapeutic INR led to warfarin dose increase. He improved clinically, with resolution of pulmonary crackles and stable vital signs, and was discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up plans.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
